name: rowan
description: Lossless green/red syntax tree library underpinning rust-analyzer

license.comment: Cargo.toml: `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`; crates.io reports the same for 0.17.0.

approach.comment: "A generic library for lossless syntax trees" (green/red trees inspired by Swift libsyntax / Roslyn). rowan is not a parser: the user writes a hand-rolled lexer+parser and feeds `GreenNodeBuilder`; rowan supplies the tree data structure, cursors, and typed-AST scaffolding. Tagged per RESEARCH.md scope ("incremental and lossless syntax-tree toolkits").

implementation.comment: Dependencies are rustc-hash, hashbrown, text-size, memoffset, countme (+ optional serde) — all pure Rust; no build script, no `cc`.

documentation.comment: No dedicated book. README points to the rust-analyzer book's syntax chapter (https://rust-analyzer.github.io/book/contributing/syntax.html) for the conceptual overview and to `examples/s_expressions.rs` as a tutorial.

first-release.comment: crates.io `created_at` 2018-10-02. Oldest version still listed on the versions endpoint is 0.5.5 (2019-06-26); earlier releases are no longer listed.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 0.17.0 published 2026-08-02. A pre-release 0.18.0-alpha.1 (2026-09-14) carries the new first-class trivia API (`leading_trivia`/`trailing_trivia`, `is_trivia`, `text_range_without_outer_trivia`). Research reflects 0.17.0 plus master.

grammar-class.comment: rowan imposes no grammar class — the parser is hand-written Rust (rust-analyzer uses hand-rolled recursive descent) that emits `start_node`/`token`/`finish_node` events to `GreenNodeBuilder`. Any parsing strategy expressible in code works.

grammar-definition.comment: Grammar lives in the user's hand-written parser; rowan only defines the `SyntaxKind`/`Language` mapping.

left-recursion.comment: Not applicable: rowan has no parsing algorithm, so left recursion is whatever the user's hand-written parser does (rust-analyzer uses Pratt-style precedence in its own parser crate, not in rowan).

ambiguity-handling.comment: Not applicable: no parsing algorithm in rowan.

backtracking.comment: Not applicable. `GreenNodeBuilder::checkpoint`/`start_node_at` lets the builder retroactively wrap already-emitted children (useful for left-associative infix parsing) but is not backtracking.

lexer-integration.comment: Any lexer works: tokens are pushed to `GreenNodeBuilder::token(kind, &str)`. The bundled example uses `m_lexer` (dev-dependency only); rust-analyzer feeds it from `ra-ap-rustc_lexer`.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: No precedence facility; only the builder `Checkpoint` helper that makes hand-written Pratt loops convenient.

unicode-aware.comment: Token text is `&str`, offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets via `text_size::TextSize`/`TextRange`, and `SyntaxText` offers char-level operations. rowan does no lexing so it has no char-matching primitives of its own.

input-types.comment: Input is a sequence of `(SyntaxKind, &str)` tokens pushed into `GreenNodeBuilder` (push API rather than a consumed slice); the source text itself is never read by rowan.

streaming-partial-input.comment: No incomplete/need-more signalling; the builder is driven synchronously to `finish()`.

zero-copy.comment: Green tokens own a copy of their text (DST allocation with header + inline text); the tree does not borrow from the source buffer. Identical tokens/nodes are deduplicated by the builder cache.

span-tracking.comment: `SyntaxNode::text_range()` / `SyntaxToken::text_range()` return `TextRange` (UTF-8 byte offsets); `token_at_offset` and `covering_element` do offset→node lookups. Line/column conversion is left to the user.

output-model.comment: Primary output is the untyped green/red lossless CST. `rowan::ast::AstNode` plus user `cast()` wrappers give a zero-cost typed view over `SyntaxNode` (as in the example's `ast_node!` macro and rust-analyzer's generated AST).

semantic-actions.comment: No actions during parsing; semantics are computed by walking/casting the finished tree (`children()`, `descendants()`, `AstNode::cast`).

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: Whitespace/comments are ordinary tokens in the tree ("whitespaces is explicit" in the example). 0.18-alpha/master adds first-class trivia helpers: `is_trivia`, `leading_trivia`/`trailing_trivia`, `text_range_without_outer_trivia`, `next_non_trivia_token`.

stateful-parsing.comment: Not applicable: rowan is not a parser driver. Any state (symbol tables, indentation) lives in the user's own hand-written parser that drives the builder.

error-recovery.comment: Not applicable / indeterminate: rowan ships no recovery mechanism. Its tree model accommodates malformed input (missing children simply absent; junk wrapped in an `ERROR`-kind node, "treated just like any other node"), but skipping/sync strategy is entirely the user's parser.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: rowan has no error type or error API. The bundled example accumulates `Vec<String>` errors alongside the tree, and rust-analyzer reports to a separate error sink, but this is user code.

expected-token-reporting.comment: Not applicable: no error type in rowan.

custom-error-types.comment: Not applicable: rowan defines no error type to substitute; errors are whatever the user's parser produces.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Not applicable: no errors are produced by rowan. `TextRange` byte spans are available on every node/token, so user-produced errors can carry byte-range spans.

contextual-error-messages.comment: Not applicable: no error mechanism in rowan.

incremental-reparsing.comment: rowan itself does not reparse. It provides the building blocks — immutable green trees with structural sharing, `SyntaxNode::replace_with(GreenNode)` (O(depth) patch producing a new root), and the builder's node/token cache — on which rust-analyzer's own `syntax` crate implements heuristic block-level incremental reparsing.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Core purpose: "lossless, or full fidelity" trees where all comments and whitespace are preserved; `SyntaxNode::text()` reconstructs the source.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language; navigation is via the cursor API (`descendants`, `token_at_offset`, `covering_element`).

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: rust-analyzer's `syntax` crate depends on `rowan` (workspace dependency). Also used by non-listed LSPs: taplo (TOML) and nil (Nix, via rnix-parser).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No independent benchmark found comparing rowan-based parsers to hand-written or other frameworks; rowan is a tree library rather than a parser, so `parse-benchmarks`-style suites do not include it.

compile-time-impact.comment: No measurement found. Small non-generic crate with five light dependencies, so likely light, but per Assessment Guidelines `null` is preferred over a guess.

allocation-strategy.comment: Each green node/token is a single reference-counted DST allocation (header + children/text inline); the builder cache deduplicates identical subtrees. Red `SyntaxNode` cursors are allocated lazily from thread-local free lists.

generated-code-size.comment: Not a generator; no code is generated.

no-std-support.comment: No `#![no_std]` and no `std` feature flag; uses thread-locals and std collections.

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in Cargo.toml (crates.io `rust_version` is null for 0.17.0), no README statement, and CI tests only the stable toolchain. Edition 2021.

unsafe-usage.comment: Crate-level `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` with `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on the `green`, `cursor`, and `arc` modules: a custom `Arc`, DST green nodes via `mem::transmute` pointer casts, and a raw-pointer/`Cell`-refcounted red-node zipper with manual free lists (~9 unsafe blocks in cursor.rs, 3 in green/node.rs). Deliberate, performance-motivated unsafe core.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: No proc-macro dependencies; `serde` derive is not used (optional `serde` with default-features off, manual impls in `serde_impls`).

dependency-count.comment: countme, hashbrown, memoffset, rustc-hash, text-size; plus optional `serde` behind the `serde1` feature (6 incl. optional). Checked 2026-09-19.

wasm-compatible.comment: No wasm target in CI and no documented statement. Nothing platform-specific in the dependency tree (pure Rust, no I/O), so it likely builds for wasm32, but untested claims are recorded as null per Assessment Guidelines.

async-friendly.comment: Red `SyntaxNode`/`SyntaxToken` cursors use `Cell` refcounts and raw pointers with thread-local free lists, so they are not `Send`. The underlying `GreenNode` is `Send + Sync` and is what rust-analyzer shares across threads.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads as of 2026-09-19 (~1.65M/month per lib.rs).

maintenance-status.comment: Substantive feature work in Sep 2026 (first-class trivia API, PRs #219/#220 merged by a rust-analyzer team member); releases 0.17.0 (Aug 2026) and 0.18.0-alpha.1 (Sep 2026). Historically slow-moving between rust-analyzer-driven bursts.

documentation-quality.comment: docs.rs reports only ~22% of items documented and there is no rowan-specific guide; the README is a few lines pointing to the rust-analyzer book's syntax chapter (a good conceptual design doc) and one commented example. Per guidelines: 2 = sparse API docs.

tutorial-book.comment: README calls `examples/s_expressions.rs` a tutorial, but it is a single commented example file; the rust-analyzer book chapter is a design overview, not a rowan guide. Does not meet the 'dedicated long-form guide' bar.

notable-users.value: rust-analyzer (syntax crate), rnix-parser / nil (Nix parser and language server), taplo (TOML toolkit and LSP)
notable-users.comment: All verified via Cargo.toml dependencies. lib.rs lists 213 direct dependents. Biome/Rome forked rowan into its own `biome_rowan` rather than depending on it.

bus-factor.comment: Hosted under the rust-analyzer GitHub org and maintained by rust-analyzer team members (original author Aleksey Kladov/matklad; recent PRs merged by ChayimFriedman2). A handful of active contributors rather than a company-backed team.
